title: Taxonomies of Hallucination in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: A formal framework for classifying, detecting, and scoring contextual vs. parametric hallucinations in high-stakes enterprise AI systems.
content:
# Taxonomies of Hallucination in RAG

## Abstract
As Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems become central to enterprise applications, standard metrics like BLEU or ROUGE fail to detect fine-grained factual drifts. This paper presents a multi-tiered taxonomy separating **Entity Substitution**, **Relation Fabrication**, and **Temporal Misalignment**.

## 1. Classification Matrix

- **Type I: Contextual Omission**: Model ignores explicitly provided context in favor of pre-trained parameters.
- **Type II: Entity Contagion**: Model swaps proper nouns or numerical attributes across retrieved documents.
- **Type III: Speculative Extrapolation**: Model predicts logical consequences without supporting premises in context.

## 2. Evaluation Methodology
Using dynamic perturbation testing, we measure hallucination rates across context lengths ranging from 1K to 128K tokens.

```text
Context Size (K Tokens)  | Type I Error | Type II Error | Overall Grounding Score
1K                       | 0.8%         | 1.2%          | 98.0%
32K                      | 2.4%         | 3.1%          | 94.5%
128K                     | 5.1%         | 6.8%          | 88.1%
```

## Conclusion
Enforcing strict schema validation at the output layer reduces Type II errors by up to 64%.
keyTakeaways: Context size scaling exponentially increases entity swap errors if unguided.
Dual-pass verification models significantly outperform single-prompt evaluation.
Taxonomy-based scoring provides actionable engineering remediations.
